title: Relative Tate determinant equals a ratio of homomorphism degrees
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $A,B$ be abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety] of the same dimension $g\geq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\lambda:A\to B$ be an isogeny [def-sc-isogeny] and $\mu\in\operatorname{Hom}_k(B,A)\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ a two-sided inverse to $\lambda$, where homomorphisms are group-scheme homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme] and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every group-scheme homomorphism $h:A\to B$, put $d(h)=\deg h$ when $h$ is an isogeny and $d(h)=0$ otherwise, with degree the order of the scheme-theoretic kernel. For every prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ one has
$$\det\bigl(V_\ell(\mu h)\mid V_\ell A\bigr)=\frac{d(h)}{\deg\lambda}\quad\text{in }\mathbf Q_\ell.$$
Here the rational Tate module and componentwise action on integral homomorphisms are [sk-def-av-tate], extended $\mathbf Q$-linearly to rational homomorphisms; the determinant is [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant], and the rational ratio is embedded in $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers].

source.place: Chapter I, Proposition 10.20, printed pp.50–52 (degree is the Tate determinant for endomorphisms), Remark 10.11, printed p.47 (rational degree), and the isogeny inverse construction in Remark 8.6, printed p.36. Relative form obtained by composing h and lambda with one common integral multiple of the rational inverse; multiplicativity of isogeny degree cancels that common factor. Zero is assigned to non-isogenies.

proof.text: First establish the integral endomorphism calculation needed below. Put $R=\operatorname{End}_k(A)$ and $E=R\otimes\mathbf Q$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-finite-free], $E$ is a finite-dimensional unital rational algebra. Let $\delta=d^0:E\to\mathbf Q$ be [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-polynomial]. It is homogeneous polynomial of degree $2g$, agrees with $d$ on $R$, and has $\delta(0)=0$. By [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-multiplicative], $d(1)=1$ and $d(ab)=d(a)d(b)$. Write $v=j(a)/n,w=j(b)/m$ using [lem-sfb-rational-tensor-fractions]. The defining denominator formula gives $\delta(vw)=(nm)^{-2g}d(ab)=\delta(v)\delta(w)$. Consequently $\delta(1)=1$ and $E\ne0$, since $\delta(0)=0$. All hypotheses of the polynomial-norm theorem are now available.

source.place: Remark 10.11 and Proposition 10.13, printed pp.47–48; Lemma 10.22, printed p.51

proof.text: For an arbitrary $a\in R$, apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-polynomial-norm] to $E,\delta,d=2g$. It gives a monic rational polynomial $P_a(t)=\delta(t1-a)$ of degree $2g$ and, for its roots $a_i$ in any splitting field, $\delta(F(a))=\prod_iF(a_i)$ for every $F\in\mathbf Q[T]$. In particular $P_a(0)=\delta(-a)=\delta(a)=d(a)$: homogeneity from [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-polynomial] gives the factor $(-1)^{2g}=1$. This is valid for nonisogenies too.

source.place: Theorem 10.9 and Remark 10.11, pp.46–47; Lemma 10.22, p.51

proof.text:
Fix $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ and put $T=V_\ell(a)$ and $Q(X)=\det(X1-T)$. By [prop-av-tate-rank] and [lem-weil-charpoly-monic-degree], $Q$ is monic of degree $2g$. Work in an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. A full invariant flag from [p-linear-triangular] gives an upper triangular matrix for $T$, whose diagonal entries $b_i$ are the roots of $Q$ counted with multiplicity: its determinant polynomial is $\prod_i(X-b_i)$. For $F\in\mathbf Z[T]$, the matrix $F(T)$ is upper triangular with diagonal $F(b_i)$, so $\det F(T)=\prod_iF(b_i)$. These determinant equalities follow directly by expanding along the triangular rows; scalar extension preserves the matrix determinant term by term. The componentwise action [sk-def-av-tate] gives $F(T)=V_\ell(F(a))$: sums, composition, identities and integer multiples agree at each torsion coordinate, hence on the inverse limit and after tensoring. Choose the roots $a_i$ of $P_a$ in the same closure. Step 2 and [lem-sfb-abelian-degree-tate-valuation], applied to the integral endomorphism $F(a)$, give
$$\left|\prod_iF(a_i)\right|_\ell=|d(F(a))|_\ell=|\det F(T)|_\ell=\left|\prod_iF(b_i)\right|_\ell.$$
The two monic polynomials have the same degree and satisfy this for every integral $F$. Thus [lem-sfb-padic-resultant-rigidity] gives $P_a=Q$ in $\mathbf Q_\ell[X]$.

source.place: Proposition 10.20 proof, printed p.52; Lemmas 10.21–10.22, p.51

proof.text:
Evaluate the equality of step 3 at zero. In a $2g$-element basis, $Q(0)=\det(-T)=(-1)^{2g}\det T=\det T$ by factoring $-1$ out of each row. Step 2 gives $P_a(0)=d(a)$. Hence
$$\det(V_\ell(a)\mid V_\ell A)=d(a)$$
for every integral endomorphism $a$, including nonisogenies. The same calculation works for every allowable $\ell$.

Apply the last clause of [lem-sfb-simple-isogeny-decomposition] to $\lambda$. It supplies an isogeny $
u:B	o A$ and $n>0$ such that $
u\lambda=[n]_A$ and $\lambda
u=[n]_B$. In the rational homomorphism spaces, $[n]=n1$ by [def-sc-mult-n], so $
u/n$ is a two-sided inverse of $\lambda$. It equals the specified $\mu$: explicitly $
u/n=(
u/n)(\lambda\mu)=((
u/n)\lambda)\mu=\mu$. Thus $\mu h=n^{-1}
u h$. The componentwise Tate action [sk-def-av-tate] and its specified rational extension give $V_\ell(\mu h)=n^{-1}V_\ell(
u h)$.

source.place: Remark 8.6, printed p.36; Remark 10.11, printed p.47

proof.text:
The geometric lemma [lem-sfb-isogeny-postcomposition-degree] applied to $(h,
u)$ gives $d(
u h)=\deg(
u)d(h)$, including $d(h)=0$. Applied to $(\lambda,
u)$ it gives $\deg(
u\lambda)=\deg(
u)\deg(\lambda)$. Since $
u\lambda=[n]_A$, [lem-sc-isogeny-facts] gives
$$\deg(
u)\deg(\lambda)=n^{2g}.$$
All degrees here use scheme-theoretic kernels. In particular $\deg\lambda>0$: its finite kernel contains the identity point and therefore has nonzero finite-dimensional coordinate algebra.

source.place: Chapter I §7, printed p.32; Theorem 7.2, p.33; Remark 8.6, p.36

proof.text:
Use the basis of size $2g$ from [prop-av-tate-rank]. Factoring $n^{-1}$ from each row and then applying step 4 to the integral endomorphism $
u h$ gives
$$\det V_\ell(\mu h)=n^{-2g}\det V_\ell(
u h)=n^{-2g}d(
u h)=n^{-2g}\deg(
u)d(h)= rac{d(h)}{\deg\lambda}.$$
The last equality uses step 6. Cancellation takes place in $\mathbf Q_\ell$, where $n$ and $\deg\lambda$ are nonzero by the canonical embedding of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Neither integer needs to be invertible in $k$. This proves the formula also when $h$ is zero or any other nonisogeny, and when either isogeny is inseparable.
